text:
Tara V.: quick heads-up: during a streaming canary I triggered a model swap from atlas-v2-64k-int4 -> atlas-v2-64k-int4-rotfix mid-generation and observed a subtle divergence in the tail of the response only when the swap happened while the KV cache was live.
Igor B.: interesting. divergence as in token shift, repeat, or semantic change? any small example?
Tara V.: small excerpt attached (rooted at the swap boundary):
```
before-swap: ... "The board unanimously agreed to proceed with the acquisition and authorized the legal team to finalize terms."
after-swap:  ... "The board unanimously agreed to proceed with the acquisitio and authorized the legal team to finalize terms."
# dropped final 'n' on acquisition, subsequent tokens seem off by one char
```
Luis F.: that looks like a byte/offset misalignment rather than a model hallucination. Did the model binary change tokenizers or rotary scaling table layout between variants?
Tara V.: no tokenizer changes. The variants differ only in a small kernel-level change to RoPE scaling (fixed a double->float truncation), and a patched KV packing path to improve throughput. The divergence only shows up when: streaming=true, swap_epoch != 0, and the serving runtime did not flush KV on swap. If we force KV flush at swap point the issue disappears.
Igor B.: reproduction steps?
Tara V.: repro: 
```
serve --model atlas-v2-64k-int4 --quant=int4 --streaming=true --swap-after-tokens=1024 --next-model atlas-v2-64k-int4-rotfix --prefill=long_disk_prefill.json --gen=512
# trigger swap during in-flight generation
```
Luis F.: so likely the in-memory KV layout (or RoPE phase table pointer) is incompatible across the two variant binaries. The runtime was trying to reuse key/value buffers to avoid memcpy during swap which could be faster but unsafe if packing/layout differs.
Igor B.: deploy-bot: can you annotate the canary and add pinned kernel/commit ids for both variants for run id 30221?
deploy-bot: annotated run 30221 with commits atlas-v2-64k-int4@c7a2 and atlas-v2-64k-int4-rotfix@d3f9. Captured runtime config and serving flags.
Tara V.: I also ran a unit-level micro-repro that simulates: 1) pack KV with old-rope-table layout, 2) resume generation feeding packed bytes into new-decoder kernel without repacking. It reproduces the single-character drop every ~50 tokens after swap.
Luis F.: that confirms layout incompatibility. Two mitigation paths: (A) always convert/repack KV on model swap, or (B) encode a lightweight header with KV-format-version and reject reuse across mismatched versions.
Igor B.: agree. short-term let's add a guarded KV-flush-on-swap option in the serving runtime and enable it for canaries. Long-term we should bake format versioning and an explicit compatibility check.
Tara V.: implemented a temporary flag --flush-kv-on-swap=true and re-ran the canary; divergence gone on three runs. Pushed small PR: https://staging-redwood/pull/3552 (contains micro-repro and unit tests).
eval-bot: ran golden-prompt suite on the after-swap responses for run 30221. Quality metrics: BLEU drop 0.8 -> 0.1 when swap happened without KV flush; after flush BLEU recovered. Logged full report under artifacts/run-30221/eval.json.
Luis F.: can we make the eval harness also simulate mid-stream swaps on CI? Seems useful to detect this class of regressions earlier.
Igor B.: good idea. add a CI job that fuzzes: swap timing, streaming on/off, and packer variant combinations. Add it to the long-running nightly matrix.
Tara V.: noted. I'll add the CI job and include the micro-repro as a unit test. Also adding a compatibility header to KV metadata is in my follow-up list.
deploy-bot: scheduled a progressive rollout hold until PR 3552 merges and the canary with --flush-kv-on-swap passes on dedicated.
Luis F.: for retrospective: file an RFC that enumerates safe/unsafe runtime invariants for buffer reuse across model switches (RoPE table shape, packer bit-width, endianness). We can prevent future issues by requiring a compatibility flag on new model builds.
Igor B.: will draft RFC with recommended compatibility checks.
Tara V.: thanks all. tagging @Luis F. for eval follow-up and @Igor B. for RFC. I'll keep the canary pinned and update once dedicated run is green. :white_check_mark:
